source_user: Give a measurement plan for validating whether KV cache helps a serving workload. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: Define the hypothesis that reusing prior K/V tensors reduces repeated prefix computation and improves decode efficiency. Sweep prompt length, generated length, and concurrency using identical request traces for cache-enabled and valid recomputation-reference runs. After warmup, repeat each point and collect TTFT separately from TPOT, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, HBM usage, cache occupancy, GPU utilization, scheduler batch size, OOMs, and rejections. Boundary condition: paging or offload can make memory movement the bottleneck, so report cache occupancy and transfer behavior with the latency result.
risks: Do not generalize from one context length or concurrency level.
evidence_required: Report repeated-run variance and the exact request distribution.

source_user: What assumptions must be stated before making a performance claim about KV cache? Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: State at least: model architecture and KV-head layout; precision and KV quantization; hardware and interconnect; serving engine and kernel versions; prompt and output-length distributions; batch policy and concurrency; scheduler, paging, offload, and prefix-sharing settings; and the latency/throughput definitions. Mechanism: caching reuses prior K/V tensors instead of recomputing prefix projections during decode. Boundary condition: the claim may fail when HBM pressure causes paging, smaller batches, eviction, or request rejection, so cache capacity and memory headroom must be measured.
risks: Performance claims without workload and engine versions are not portable.
evidence_required: Record all assumptions and raw metrics before comparing configurations.

source_user: What assumptions must be stated before making a performance claim about KV cache? Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: Specify the model's layer count, attention type, KV heads, head dimension, precision, and maximum context; the serving engine, kernels, GPU type, and memory allocator; request-length distribution, concurrency, batch/scheduler policy, and whether prefix sharing or offload is enabled; and whether the metric is TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency, or tokens/s. Mechanism: cached K/V avoids repeated prefix projection. Boundary condition: at high concurrency, cache memory can limit admission or batch size and reverse an apparent throughput benefit.
risks: TTFT and TPOT represent different phases and must not be conflated.

source_user: What assumptions must be stated before making a performance claim about KV cache? Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: Before claiming a benefit, state the workload's prompt/output lengths, concurrency, arrival pattern, batch policy, target latency percentile, and throughput definition. Also state model architecture, KV-head count, precision, GPU and interconnect, engine/kernel versions, cache paging/quantization/prefix-sharing options, and baseline configuration. Mechanism: cache reuse removes repeated K/V computation for the already processed prefix. Boundary condition: allocator fragmentation, workspace memory, or other resident buffers may leave less HBM than the theoretical cache formula predicts.
risks: The theoretical cache budget omits implementation overhead.
evidence_required: Include HBM peak and fragmentation/allocator statistics when available.

source_user: What assumptions must be stated before making a performance claim about KV cache? Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: State the workload, including prompt length, output length, concurrency, arrival rate, batching, and requested latency percentile; the model's layers, KV heads, head dimension, precision, and context limit; the GPU, engine, kernels, and cache policy; and the comparison baseline. Mechanism: cached K/V tensors are reused by later decode steps, avoiding prefix recomputation. evidence_required: Record effective cache capacity and request admission behavior.

source_user: Explain how KV cache changes between training and inference. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: During autoregressive inference, a KV cache stores prior tokens' attention K/V tensors and reuses them at each decode step, so only the new token's projections are added. Standard teacher-forced training usually processes a complete sequence in parallel and constructs attention intermediates for the training forward pass; it does not maintain one persistent per-request decode cache across generated steps. Boundary condition: specialized training methods such as packed sequences, chunked attention, or prefix caching may change memory behavior, so the exact implementation must be stated.
risks: Training memory still includes activations and attention-related state; it is not described by inference KV-cache capacity alone.

source_user: Explain how KV cache changes between training and inference. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: Inference retains K/V tensors for each active sequence and appends one token at a time, avoiding repeated prefix computation. Ordinary full-sequence training uses teacher forcing and builds a forward/backward graph for the batch; it normally does not maintain a persistent per-request decode cache. Boundary condition: gradient checkpointing, packed sequences, flash-attention variants, and chunked training change training activation memory, so training memory and inference KV-cache memory must be budgeted separately.
risks: Exact training memory depends strongly on attention implementation and sequence packing.

source_user: Explain how KV cache changes between training and inference. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: Inference uses an incremental cache: after processing a prompt, the server retains each layer's K/V for every active sequence and appends K/V for each generated token. This supports one-token-at-a-time decoding without recomputing the full prefix. Full-sequence training instead uses teacher forcing, computes the batch's token interactions in a forward/backward graph, and retains or recomputes activations for gradients. Boundary condition: training can use checkpointing, packed sequences, or chunked attention, while inference cache memory is governed by active-token count and concurrency; the two budgets must be measured separately.
risks: Training and inference may share kernels but have different memory lifetimes and objectives.
evidence_required: Report separate training activation memory and inference cache occupancy.
